page.title: Native Review - SMS Pet Design System

content.title: SMS Pet design system review
content.body: This review page turns the current website into a reusable native Elementor foundation before we redesign the dedicated service pages. It keeps the warm orange-and-cream personality, playful pet energy, and animal-specific service accents already present on the live site.
content.headingSample: Warm, mobile-first grooming pages with clearer structure
content.bodySample: Inter is the dominant live-site typeface, so this draft centers it across headings, body copy, cards, and calls to action. The decorative script feeling from the current homepage can stay optional later as a small accent layer, not the structural system.

content.title: Animal-specific accents on one shared page system
content.body: The live site already uses the same overall layout logic across grooming pages. This review keeps that consistency, then sharpens each page with a distinct but compatible accent color so the future service pages feel related without becoming repetitive.

items.title: Dog Grooming
items.body: High-energy, confidence-led sections anchored by the orange CTA system and a bright green support accent for pricing, proof, and action moments.

items.title: Cat Grooming
items.body: A calmer premium variation using the existing blue accent for pricing and card moments while staying inside the same typography and spacing system.

items.title: Bird Grooming
items.body: A lighter mint-accent service direction that still shares the same hero, service-card, process, and booking structure as the other animal pages.

items.title: Rabbit Grooming
items.body: A softer coral accent for gentle-care messaging, paired with the same reusable booking and package patterns so maintenance stays simple in Elementor.

content.title: What the current site is already doing well
content.body: The existing homepage sets a useful sequence for the redesign work ahead: playful hero, quick trust/process explanation, service discovery, testimonials, and a direct booking prompt. The next phase should preserve that conversion rhythm while cleaning up typography consistency, pricing-card clarity, and reusable section patterns across each service page.

content.title: Photography and illustration style to carry forward
content.body: Rounded, cheerful pet imagery and service illustrations should keep supporting the warm, approachable tone. The redesign work should reuse this friendly visual language while simplifying the layouts around it.

images.caption: Playful hero illustration and pet grouping

content.title: What carries forward before the new service pages

items.question: What should remain from the current website?
items.answer: The orange primary actions, warm cream surfaces, approachable pet-focused tone, and simple booking-first flow are all worth preserving.

items.question: What should be tightened up in the redesign phase?
items.answer: Typography should be normalized around Inter, service cards should feel more consistent, and each animal page should reuse one cleaner pricing and add-on structure.

items.question: Why make a design-system review page first?
items.answer: It gives us one live reference point to approve before we redesign the individual dog, cat, bird, and rabbit service pages as separate conversion pages.

content.title: Approved foundation for the upcoming service-page redesigns
content.body: Once this review page feels right, we can use it as the live reference system for the separate Dog, Cat, Bird, and Rabbit redesigns you want to tackle next.
